A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Squirrel Benchmark study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite formatting changes and reordered appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM evaluations, SFT and agent experiments in Section 5, plus training-dynamics analyses and debugging case studies in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports human validation of Graph Match agreement and model rankings in Appendix D.1.4.

M1.justification: The benchmark-construction pipeline, bug injection, EM/GM/MB evaluation, three SFT approaches and agent procedure remain unchanged. Removed implementation disclosures and the added metric-validation study do not establish changes to these procedures.

E1.justification: Both retain 469 Squirrel-Syntax and 516 Squirrel-Semantic Hive/Spark SQL tasks with the same domain coverage. The three training-data components, including BIRD/Spider-derived examples, are unchanged. The human metric check introduces no documented new task or domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 and Figures 4–5 retain the same evaluated models, SFT variants and agent comparisons. Qwen-2.5-Instruct remains in Table 2 despite its omission from the shortened Appendix D.2 roster; no changed model-baseline set is documented.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1.4 adds human evaluation on 300 samples and a ranking comparison using 100 samples for each of three models. Whether these samples overlap is unspecified. Existing training settings, inference settings and benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted analysis of GM reliability against expert judgments and human-derived model rankings. The existing training-step analysis in Figure 9 and error case studies in Figures 10–11 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: There is no added or revised repeated-run information, random-seed reporting, confidence interval or significance test. The new human-agreement percentage and ranking consistency are point findings, without accompanying uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports over 68% GM agreement with expert judgments and matching GM/human rankings for three models in Appendix D.1.4. Existing tabulated and plotted results remain unchanged, including Claude-4-Sonnet's 36.46% and 32.17% GM scores in Table 2.

T1.justification: The task definition, complexity measure, dataset-construction expressions and EM/GM/MB definitions in Equations 1–7 are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, automated construction, execution-free evaluation, LLM capability-gap and four solution-strategy claims. The assertion of strong correlation with practical debugging performance also remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.1.4 newly discusses GM false negatives and argues that they affect models fairly while preserving rankings. V2 also removes the observation that Claude struggles despite having generated the benchmark. Appendix F retains the principal synthetic-data, reference-solution and dialect limitations.

D1.justification: V2 removes the identification of Claude-4-Sonnet at temperature zero for synthesis, Appendix C's internal seed-source, de-identification and validation details, and the 32 NVIDIA H20 GPU disclosure. It also deletes the planned public-release and proprietary-training-data disclosures. Although prompts, SFT hyperparameters and software versions remain, these omissions substantially reduce construction provenance and reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 removes the CoCA citation by Zhu et al. (2024) from the introduction and bibliography. Most other reference changes update publication or author metadata for retained works, including DM-SFT, SWE-SQL and Fullstack Bench; the overall research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 condenses the abstract and agent overview, rewrites the LLM-use disclosure, updates affiliations and changes the disclosure sections. It removes the appendix contents page and moves prompts ahead of taxonomy and examples. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column main text with a two-column layout, restyles titles, headers and contribution boxes, and substantially resizes and repositions figures and tables, especially Figures 4–5. All 13 figures and four tables remain, with broad reflow of appendix displays.

improvement.justification: The new human check addresses an important metric-validity concern, but unspecified model identities, sampling procedures and individual scores limit the strength of that gain. Meanwhile, v2 removes substantial generator, seed-provenance, hardware and data-access disclosures available in v1. The added but incompletely documented validation and reduced reproducibility have competing effects whose net impact on overall quality is not reliably clear.
